newsitem.title: FRANCE: S. Korea's Daewoo establishes fourth French plant.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea's Daewoo establishes fourth French plant.

text.p: South Korean giant Daewoo Electronics, still keen on France despite the public rejection of its bid for state-owned Thomson Multimedia, said on Wednesday it was setting up a fourth plant in eastern France.

Chairman Soon-Hoon Bae said the group would invest 1.74 billion francs ($302.1 million) to set up a plant making television and computer screens in the town of Thionville, creating 700 jobs in the next three years, the French industry ministry said.

"Daewoo thus confirms the industrial strategy of its presence in France which represent 1,200 jobs. Thanks to this project and the expansion of its French plants announced in 1996, Daewoo will employ 2,700 people in France in the coming years," the ministry said in a statement.
Last year Daewoo teamed up with Lagardere Group in a bid for the state-owned Thomson SA group.
Lagardere had agreed to sell money-losing Thomson Multimedia (TMM) to Daewoo and keep Thomson's defence electronics unit, Thomson-CSF.
The deal was initially approved by the French government but scrapped after the independent Privatisation Commission objected to the terms.
The government's decision to cancel the sale, which also followed a public outcry tinged with xenophobia, mushroomed into a diplomatic incident between the Seoul and Paris governments.

Chairman Soon-Hoon Bae said in a French newspaper interview last month that Daewoo was still interested in bidding for Thomson Multimedia, which is due to be privatised separately from the rest of the group after an 11-billion franc state recapitalisation.
The French government on Tuesday appointed Thierry Breton, a former senior manager at recently-privatised Compagnie des Machines Bull, to head TMM and prepare its sale.
It said TMM would be sold gradually through the opening up of its capital, much the way Bull was privatised. It has already launched the privatisation of the profitable Thomson-CSF.
